queries.hook: I lost my job. Inside, something doesn't sit right and I can't name it, and I don't know how to carry it.

hook.speaker: Bharat
hook.setting: Bharat, urged by his teacher and mother to accept the throne, explains why he cannot.
hook.sanskrit: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
hook.line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
hook.translation: You give me simple advice, the kind that would do me good if I followed it. Though I understand it well, my heart is not at peace.
hook.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

alternates.speaker: Rama
alternates.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
alternates.line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
alternates.translation: Though my heart is packed tight with the stones of life's sorrows, I don't let my tears fall, only out of fear of what my own people would think.
alternates.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
alternates.misuse: Holding tears in is not strength. Rama's healing began when he finally said it aloud.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
alternates.sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
alternates.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
alternates.translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
alternates.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verse.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verse.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: You wake at six because your mind is still spinning scenarios. Let the morning be quiet. The world of trouble shrinks when you stop feeding it.
verse.scene_line: You still wake at six, but your mind no longer has to clutch the day.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
the swelling is traced to the spinning, which can be stopped

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: On this path, no beginning is lost and no harm results. Even a small amount of this practice protects from great fear. The tradition reads this as a path of action where every step forward counts, and even a little effort shields one from the fear of birth and death.
verse.for_you: You may feel stuck, but no sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of this practice shields you from great fear.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing you did today that did not fail.

why: Even a little of this path protects from great fear.
a small sincere effort already protects

verse.speaker: The river Ganga (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: The Ocean asks the rivers why they uproot great trees but never the humble cane; Ganga answers.
verse.sanskrit: वेतसो वेगमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा नमति नापरे / स च वेगे ह्यतिक्रान्ते स्थानमापद्यते पुनः
verse.line: The cane bends when the flood comes, and stands up again once it has passed.
verse.translation: The cane, seeing the flood coming, bends; no other tree does. And once the force has passed, it stands back up in its place.
verse.why: Bend with the flood and you stand again after it passes.
verse.misuse: Bending under pressure is not giving up your values.

prasang.title: The river and the reeds
prasang.summary: The Ocean asks the rivers why they uproot great trees but never the reeds. Ganga answers: the reed bends when the flood comes and stands again after; the rigid tree breaks.
prasang.story_hook: The rivers tore down mighty trees every monsoon, yet never the humble reeds on their banks.
prasang.lesson: Bend with the flood and you stand again after it passes.

verse.try_today: Notice one rigid habit today and let it bend slightly without force.

why: Shows a way through overwhelming force that does not require breaking
Reading the time and the strength of what is coming

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: दिवसेनैव तत्कुर्याद्येन रात्रौ सुखं वसेत् / अष्टमासेन तत्कुर्याद्येन वर्षाः सुखं वसेत् पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धः सुखं वसेत् / यावज्जीवं तु तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत्
verse.line: Do today what lets you sleep tonight, and in youth what lets you rest in old age.
verse.translation: Do during the day what lets you sleep in peace at night; do in the eight dry months what lets you live comfortably through the rains. Do in youth what makes old age comfortable, and do all your life what brings peace after death.
verse.why: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

verse.for_you: You wake at six and the house is empty of work. The morning asks you to choose one small thing that will let you rest. Let that choice be enough for today.
verse.try_today: Before you sleep, notice one thing you did today that brought you peace.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of a new morning, while Vidura stands beside a king who cannot sleep.

why: Each stretch of time prepares the next
Choose today's act by how it will sit at night

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verse.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verse.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.try_today: Notice one small choice you make today that is not driven by fear.

why: Courage and steadiness are the wheels of the chariot that wins; do not let fear decide.
Composure for those who depend on one

story.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
story.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
story.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
